The Respondents are the Distribution Licensees, Power Departments and Transmission Licensees, mainly beneficiaries of the Southern Region, who are procuring transmission services from the Petitioner. 5. The Petitioner has served a copy of the Petition on the Respondents, and notice of this Petition has also been published in the newspaper in accordance with Section 64 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as “the Act). However, no comments or suggestions have been received from the general public in response to the aforesaid notice published in the newspaper by the Petitioner. 6. The hearing in this matter was held on 27.2.2026 and the order was reserved. This order is being passed considering the submissions made by the Petitioner vide 7. Having heard the learned Counsel of the Respondent No. 1 and the representatives of the Petitioner and perused the material on record, we proceed to dispose of the Petition in the succeeding paragraphs of this order. 11. We have considered the Petitioner’s submissions and noted that the capital cost has been claimed by the Petitioner with respect to the transmission asset based on the 24. The Petitioner further submitted that the Respondent’s submission regarding imprudence in the original estimates due to the increase in Plant and Machinery Cost is unfounded, as the procurement has been carried out through a transparent beneficiaries, contracts for procurement is packaged by grouping equipment, goods, works, services in optimum quantities. In the instant Petition, considering the small bid size of the subject scope of work, it has been has been clubbed with other projects under implementation at the relevant time to obtain better competitive prices. The Petitioner also submitted that in the process of achieving such competitive pricing, a marginal delay of 127 days has been encountered. which was beyond the control of Petitioner and has accordingly prayed for condonation of the said delay. 31. TNPDCL in its reply vide affidavit dated 19.2.2026, submitted that the delay is attributable to the Petitioner’s own procurement and contract award decisions, which were entirely within the Petitioner’s control and do not qualify as uncontrollable factors under Regulation 22(2) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. It was further submitted that such decisions are foreseeable and form part of normal project execution risks, which are required to be managed within the approved implementation schedule and cannot be passed on to the beneficiaries. 32. The Petitioner in its rejoinder vide affidavit dated 13.3.2026, has submitted that the claims made by the Respondent are misconceived and erroneous.
